issues: A white line-art icon with a black outline stood on an 8px grey floor bar; it looked like a placeholder, not an app in a Dock
The four hops were timed by frame count with no relation to height, and the landing squash sprang back linearly with no weight
The 'camera is drawn in' beat was just an 8% global zoom; nothing around the icon receded, so the shift of attention did not read
The closing panel used 13–20px text that could not be read, and the last frame was not a poster
changes: Sand look (warm afternoon beige, terracotta): two slanted blind-light shafts on the back wall, a frosted cream Dock cropped by both frame edges, and desaturated neighbour icons
The hero is now a 360px calendar icon 'Daybook' (terracotta FRI header, big 17), far more recognisable than a generic bell

Four hops follow real ballistics: 0.35 to 1.2 icon heights with airtime proportional to the square root of height (14/18/22/26f); velocity stretch in the air, a 2f contact squash that grows to 1.2x wide by 0.8x tall, a damped-cosine settle on the last landing, and a soft ripple plus specks at each touchdown
Being drawn in is acted out: from the second hop the neighbours rack out of focus and desaturate, and the highest hop gets a smooth 8% push-in

On landing a terracotta badge pops and the running dot lights, then the feature panel springs out of the icon's top-right with a 68px title and three staggered 32–36px agenda rows; 156f, ending on a complete feature poster
